subject: Re: Post-demo: telemetry & vendor sharing checklist and retention constraints
messages:

Subject: Post-demo: telemetry & vendor sharing checklist and retention constraints

Marcus — thanks again for the demo earlier. NovaRetail liked the latency profile and the idea of a predictable dedicated tier, but my security team flagged a few follow-ups we need before we can move to procurement: 

1) Subprocessor and telemetry vendor list — who receives any runtime telemetry or aggregated usage metrics?
2) Data residency options for both inference outputs and logs (we operate in US + EU).
3) What types of data you consider PII by default and whether prompts are stored/searched.
4) Retention windows and the ability to configure them per customer.
5) Verification of logging controls (access logs, change history) and any third-party access via the marketplace.

Attached is our high-level security intake (I’ll share a full questionnaire if helpful). Could you send a short checklist and any DPA/DPA redline guidance we can hand to procurement? If it helps, we can set a 30–45 minute follow-up with our infosec folks next week.

Best,
Sara
Head of Product Security, NovaRetail

Attachments: NovaRetail-InfoSec-Intake-brief.pdf (1 page stub)

From: marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>

Date: 2027-02-28T18:04:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: telemetry & vendor sharing checklist and retention constraints

Sara — really appreciate the clear list. Quick recap and what I’m attaching: 

Recap (high-level)
- Redwood supports hosted, dedicated (reserved GPU pools), and private/VPC deployments.
- By default we collect operational telemetry (latency, error rates, token counts, model selection) but we do not persist customer prompts in searchable logs unless the customer opts into debug capture.
- We use a small set of subprocessors for infrastructure and telemetry (cloud provider, metrics vendor, CDN). We share an attached Subprocessors Matrix (Redwood-Subprocessors-Matrix-v1.2.xlsx) and an annotated DPA draft (Redwood-DPA-annotated-draft.pdf).

Short answers to your specific questions:
1) Subprocessors & telemetry vendors: listed in the matrix. For hosted customers we stream aggregated metrics to a telemetry vendor for product reliability; for Dedicated/Private customers we can gate or disable that sharing.
2) Data residency: we can pin model outputs and logs to region-specific storage in our Dedicated and Private offerings. Hosted customers can select region; EU data residency options available via our EU region.
3) PII & prompt storage: default policy is no persistent prompt storage. If debug/logging is enabled, prompts are stored encrypted and access is audited. For any PII class your team defines, we can provide configuration options and redaction guidance.
4) Retention: default telemetry retention is 90 days; longer retention is configurable per contract for Dedicated/Private.
5) Logging controls: we maintain access logs, role-based access, and can provide audit extracts on request; marketplace integrations are opt-in and documented in the matrix.

Next steps I propose:
- Monica (cc’d) will send a compact checklist with fields NovaRetail needs filled;
- We’ll provide a redline-capable DPA and a short annotation explaining each subprocessor’s function;
- Schedule a 30–45 minute security deep-dive next week (monica + grace + your security contact).

I’ve attached the matrix and the DPA draft. Please let me know the three items you’d like us to prioritize in the deep-dive.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Marcus.lin@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0187

Date: 2027-03-01T08:12:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: telemetry & vendor sharing checklist and retention constraints

Hi Sara — Monica from Redwood InfoSec here. I dropped an annotated subprocessors matrix into the attachments and pulled out the items I think matter most to NovaRetail:

Key points from the matrix (summary):
- Cloud infra: primary compute in GCP (us-west1) for hosted; EU compute available in europe-west2. Cloud provider access is restricted to infra ops and encrypted at rest.
- Telemetry vendors: we use Datadog for metrics and an internal event-aggregator for token accounting. Datadog receives only aggregated time-series metrics (no prompt text).
- Marketplace flows: when a customer enables a marketplace integration (e.g., third-party analytics), telemetry is routed only if the customer authorizes the integration; marketplace providers do not get raw prompts by default.
- PII handling: we classify PII per customer definition. Typical PII fields we see: email, phone, shipping address, payment identifier. We can add automatic redaction pipelines for prompt captures on Dedicated/Private plans.
- Retention options: operational metrics (default 90 days), aggregated billing logs (365 days), debug traces (configurable, default 30 days, can be disabled).

What I need from NovaRetail to finalize the matrix:
- Confirm the PII classes you want treated as sensitive (exact fields).
- Confirm which retention buckets (30/90/365) you want enforced by contract.
- Indicate whether marketplace integrations should be allowed to receive aggregated telemetry or must be blocked entirely.

I’ll prepare an exportable CSV of the matrix with column-level descriptions for your procurement team. Happy to join the call Marcus suggested.

Cheers,
Monica Patel
Security & Trust, Redwood Inference
Attachments: Redwood-Subprocessors-Matrix-v1.2.xlsx (annotated), subprocessors-summary.csv (stub)

Date: 2027-03-01T09:20:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: telemetry & vendor sharing checklist and retention constraints

Team — thanks for the quick turnaround. A few clarifications from our security review: 

1) PII scope: we require that email addresses, full shipping addresses, and order-level identifiers that can be linked to individuals be treated as PII. Order ids that are purely numeric but tied to personal data count as PII.
2) Retention buckets: procurement prefers 30 days for debug traces, 90 days for operational telemetry, and 365 days for billing/audit logs. We may request a shorter window for any data flagged as GPO/health related.
3) Third-party telemetry: we require confirmation that any telemetry shipped to vendors is pseudonymized (hashed) and contains no prompt text or customer-submitted content. Can you confirm hashing and salt policies?
4) Marketplace: marketplace integrations must be explicitly approved by NovaRetail and documented in the contract. Any marketplace access to aggregated telemetry needs to be opt-in and auditable.

I’m attaching our full InfoSec questionnaire for your legal team to review. If you can provide the hashed telemetry examples and the subprocessor contact/role mapping, we can route the DPA redlines through procurement.

Regards,
NovaRetail Security

Attachments: NovaRetail-InfoSec-Questionnaire.pdf (15 pages)
